en: last day of the lunar month

examples.ko: 음력 그믐에 할머니 댁에 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to visit Grandma's house on the last day of the lunar month.
Around the end of the lunar month, the moon is hardly visible.

examples.ko: 음력 그믐날 밤에는 하늘이 아주 어두워요.
examples.en: On the last night of the lunar month, the sky is very dark.

examples.ko: 그믐달이 새벽 하늘에 가늘게 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A thin waning crescent hangs in the dawn sky.
On a moonless night at month's end, the stars are easier to see.
It was the end of the month, so the road was pitch dark.

explain: 음력 한 달의 마지막 날이에요. 이날 밤에는 달이 거의 안 보여요. 달이 가장 둥근 '보름'과 짝으로 외우세요. 그믐 무렵에 뜨는 가는 달은 '그믐달'이에요.

phrases.example: 그믐날 밤에는 달이 거의 안 보여요.
phrases.en: On the last night of the lunar month, you can hardly see the moon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음력 한 달의 마지막 날을 날짜처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the last day of the lunar month as a date.
phrases.en_equiv: the last day of the lunar month

phrases.en: A thin waning moon hung in the sky at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그믐 무렵에 뜨는 가는 달이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The thin moon that appears around the end of the lunar month.

phrases.example: 그믐에는 달이 안 보이고 보름에는 달이 둥글어요.
phrases.en: The moon is invisible at the month's end and round at mid-month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 반대되는 날이라 짝으로 같이 외우면 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: They are opposite days, so they're easy to learn as a pair.

explain_en: It is the last day of a lunar month, and the moon is barely visible that night. Learn it as a pair with '보름', when the moon is fullest. The thin moon seen around then is called '그믐달'.

examples.en: On weekends I get up fairly late and have brunch.
I left home rather late and was late for the appointment.

examples.ko: 그는 느지막이 공부를 시작했지만 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: He started studying rather late in life, but he worked hard.
Today you can come to work a bit late.
I had a late lunch and then took a walk.
My mother got married rather late.

explain: '늦게'와 비슷하지만 서두르지 않는 여유로운 느낌이 있어요. 일어나다, 나가다, 먹다 같은 동작과 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.en: On Sundays I eat breakfast late and unhurried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 대화에서 자연스럽게 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, a natural form in conversation.

phrases.en: Today you can go to work a bit late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 늦게 나가도 되는 상황에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits situations where going late without rushing is fine.

phrases.en: It's Sunday, so I ate lunch late and unhurried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 평소보다 늦게 먹는 여유로운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a relaxed feeling of eating later than usual without rushing.

explain_en: It is similar to '늦게' (late), but it feels unhurried and relaxed. It is often paired with actions like waking up, going out and eating.

examples.en: I have an exam the week after next.
I plan to move the month after next.
Please get off at the station after the next one.
The stop after the next is my house.
I have to give a presentation in the class after next.
When should we set the appointment after the next one?

explain: '다음'의 다음을 뜻하며 주, 달, 역, 차례처럼 순서가 있는 말 앞에 써요. 날짜는 '모레'나 '글피'처럼 따로 있는 말도 있어요. '다다음 주'는 '다음 주'보다 한 주 뒤예요.

phrases.en: I'm meeting my friend the week after next.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다음 주'보다 한 주 뒤를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to one week later than '다음 주' (next week).

phrases.en: I'm going on a trip the month after next.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다음 달'의 다음 달을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the month after next month.

phrases.en: Please get off at the station after next.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 다음 역이 아니라 그다음 역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not the very next station but the one after it.

explain_en: It means the one after '다음' (next), and is placed before ordered nouns like weeks, months, stations and turns. For days there are separate words like '모레' and '글피'. '다다음 주' is one week after '다음 주'.

examples.en: It's hard to improve your skills in a short time.

examples.ko: 단시일 내에 일을 끝내야 해서 바빠요.
examples.en: I have to finish the work in a short time, so I'm busy.

examples.ko: 살은 단시일에 빼면 다시 찌기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you lose weight in a short time, it's easy to gain it back.

examples.ko: 이 프로젝트는 단시일에 끝낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: This project can't be finished in a short time.
Many people applied within a short period.
There's no way to learn Korean in a short time.

explain: '단시일에', '단시일 내에'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 써요. 반대는 '장기간'이고, 말할 때는 '짧은 시간에', '금방'이라고 더 자주 해요.

phrases.en: It's hard to get results within a short time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정해진 짧은 기간 안에'라는 뜻으로 글과 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means 'within a short period', often used in writing and news.

phrases.en: I want to finish this job in a short time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 시간에 일을 마친다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means finishing a task quickly.
phrases.en_equiv: to finish in a short time

phrases.en: My Korean improved a lot in a short time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단시일에'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 이 표현을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '단시일에', and more common in speech.

explain_en: It nearly always appears in set forms like '단시일에' or '단시일 내에'. The opposite is '장기간', and in casual speech people more often say '짧은 시간에' or '금방'.

en: to be dense; to be packed with; to be tightly packed

examples.ko: 책장에 책이 빽빽해서 더 넣을 곳이 없어요.
examples.en: The bookshelf is packed, so there is no room for more.
The trees in the forest stood thick and close together.
My schedule this week is packed.

examples.ko: 공책에 작은 글씨가 빽빽한 줄로 가득해요.
examples.en: The notebook is full of densely packed small writing.
The subway at rush hour was packed with people.

examples.ko: 나무가 빽빽하면 햇빛이 잘 안 들어와요.
examples.en: If the trees are too dense, sunlight hardly comes in.

explain: '많다'는 양을 말하고, 빽빽하다는 사이에 틈이 없이 꽉 찬 모양이에요. 나무, 글씨, 사람, 일정처럼 여러 개가 붙어 있을 때 써요. 반대는 '드문드문하다'이고, 일정에 쓰면 쉴 틈이 없다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I got lost in the dense forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 틈 없이 꽉 찬 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something tightly packed before a noun.

phrases.en: My schedule is packed this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉴 틈 없이 할 일이 많을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is no free time.

phrases.en: The books aren't packed tightly, so they are easy to take out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틈이 있다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says there is some space.

explain_en: Tightly packed — things crammed with no gaps, like books or trees (빽빽하다) 많다 is about amount, while 빽빽하다 describes things packed with no gap between them. It is used for trees, writing, people, and schedules. The opposite is 드문드문하다, and for a schedule it means there is no time to rest.

t90.ax: My schedule this week is packed.

en: to be scheduled; to be due

examples.en: The meeting is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.
It ended earlier than the scheduled time.

examples.ko: 수리가 다음 주로 예정되어서 가게를 쉴 거예요.
examples.en: The repairs are scheduled for next week, so the shop will be closed.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 올가을에 개봉하는 것으로 예정됐어요.
examples.en: That movie is slated to open this fall.

examples.ko: 새 건물의 완공은 내년으로 예정되어 있어요.
examples.en: The new building is scheduled to be completed next year.
Two performances were scheduled.

explain: 일이 앞으로 있을 것으로 정해져 있다는 말이에요. 보통 '예정되어 있다'로 쓰고, '예정이다'와 거의 같게 쓰여요. 사람이 주어일 때는 '~할 예정이에요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The performance is scheduled for 7 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예정돼 있다'의 원래 형태로, 조금 더 격식 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of '예정돼 있다', slightly more formal.

phrases.en: Please check the scheduled plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 정해 둔 것을 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for something set in advance.

phrases.en: Class starts as scheduled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획한 그대로 된다는 뜻의 부사어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverbial phrase meaning exactly as planned.

explain_en: Passive; something is set for a certain time (수업이 예정되다) It says something is already set to happen in the future. It is usually used as '예정되어 있다' and works almost like '예정이다'. When a person is the subject, '~할 예정이에요' sounds more natural.

dis.h: set for a certain time; scheduled
gh: general word for being planned out
designed as an organized project or event

examples.en: When I grow up, I want to become a doctor.
Come and visit again sometime.
I'm busy now, so let's talk later.

examples.ko: 이담에 돈을 모으면 세계 여행을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: When I save up money someday, I'll travel around the world.

examples.ko: 오늘은 바쁘니까 이담으로 미루면 안 될까요?
examples.en: I'm busy today, so could we put it off until another time?

examples.ko: 이담부터는 약속 시간을 꼭 지켜 주세요.
examples.en: From next time on, please be sure to keep the appointment time.

explain: '이다음'의 준말이고, 주로 말할 때 '이담에'의 모양으로 써요. '다음에'와 비슷하지만 막연히 앞으로 올 어느 때를 가리키는 느낌이 있어요. 격식을 차리는 자리나 글에서는 '다음에'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이담에 시간 나면 같이 영화 봐요.
phrases.en: When you have time later, let's watch a movie together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해지지 않은 앞으로의 어느 때를 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual reference to an unspecified time in the future.

phrases.example: 이담에 어른이 되면 세계 여행을 할 거예요.
phrases.en: When I grow up, I'll travel the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼 훗날의 꿈이나 계획을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits talk of distant dreams or plans.

phrases.en: Next time, I'll definitely treat you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '는'을 붙여서 이번과 달리 다음에는 하겠다는 뜻을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '는' stresses 'unlike this time, next time'.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of '이다음' and is mostly used in speech as '이담에'. It is similar to '다음에' (next time), but feels like pointing to some vague time in the future. In formal settings or writing, '다음에' sounds more natural.

examples.en: At the start of the new year, families gather and do the New Year bow.
I had a rough time with a cold right from the start of the year.
Since it is the start of the year, shops close for a few days.
Next week is the start of the year. Are you going anywhere?
I plan to go down to my hometown during the New Year holiday.
The tteokguk you eat at the start of the year tastes the best.

explain: '연초'는 한 해의 처음 무렵을 넓게 말할 때 쓰고, '정초'는 설을 전후한 새해 첫머리 느낌이 더 강해요. '정초부터', '정초에는'처럼 새해 첫 며칠의 분위기를 말할 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: At the start of the year, I eat tteokguk with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해 첫머리의 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the very beginning of the new year.
phrases.en_equiv: at the start of the year

phrases.en: It snowed a lot from the very start of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해 시작부터 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things that happen right from the new year's start.
phrases.en_equiv: from the start of the year

phrases.en: At the beginning of the year, I make new plans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 처음 무렵을 더 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers more broadly to the early part of the year.

explain_en: '연초' refers broadly to the early part of the year, while '정초' feels more like the very first days around the Lunar New Year. It fits phrases like '정초부터' and '정초에는' when you talk about the mood of those first days.

examples.en: Learning developed greatly in the middle of the Joseon period.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 중기 목표부터 정해야 해요.
examples.en: For this plan, we have to set the mid-term goals first.
That patient's illness has entered the middle stage.
The company announced a three-year mid-term strategy.

examples.ko: 이 식물은 성장 중기에 물이 많이 필요해요.
examples.en: This plant needs a lot of water in the middle of its growth.

examples.ko: 중기 예보를 보면 다음 주에도 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: According to the medium-range forecast, it looks like it will rain next week too.

explain: '초기'와 '말기' 사이의 시기가 중기예요. 역사에서는 '조선 중기'처럼 시대 이름 뒤에 붙고, 계획에서는 '단기-중기-장기'로 나눠 써요. '중반'은 흐름의 가운데 부분을 더 가볍게 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: The company made a three-year mid-term plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 짧지도 길지도 않은 기간의 계획에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a plan that is neither short nor long in length.

phrases.en: I saw a painting from the mid-Joseon period at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시대 이름 뒤에 붙여 그 시대의 가운데 시기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached to an era name to mean the middle part of that era.
phrases.en_equiv: the middle of the Joseon period

phrases.example: 목표를 단기, 중기, 장기로 나눠 보세요.
phrases.en: Try dividing your goals into short, mid, and long term.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 목표를 기간에 따라 나눌 때 세 단어를 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The three words are used together to split plans by time span.

explain_en: 중기 is the period between 초기 (early) and 말기 (late). In history it follows an era name, like 조선 중기, and in planning it is part of 단기-중기-장기 (short-, mid-, long-term). 중반 is a lighter word for the middle part of something.

en: to visit someone who cannot go out

examples.ko: 입대한 친구를 면회하러 새벽부터 기차를 탔어요.
examples.en: I took a train from dawn to visit my friend who joined the army.

examples.ko: 병원에서는 환자를 면회하는 시간이 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has set times for visiting patients.

examples.ko: 삼십 분만 면회해도 되는지 간호사에게 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked the nurse if I could visit for just thirty minutes.

examples.ko: 이 병원에서 환자를 면회하려면 먼저 예약해야 해요.
examples.en: To visit a patient at this hospital, you have to book first.

examples.ko: 어제 동생을 면회하고 맛있는 걸 사 줬어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I visited my younger sibling and bought them something tasty.

examples.ko: 감염 예방 때문에 지금은 직접 면회할 수 없어요.
examples.en: To prevent infection, you can't visit in person right now.

explain: '만나다'와 달리 군대, 병원, 교도소처럼 마음대로 나올 수 없는 곳에 있는 사람을 찾아가 만날 때 써요. 보통 '면회(를) 가다/오다'라고 하고, '면회 시간'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 주말에 군대에 있는 동생을 면회 가요.
phrases.en: On the weekend, I'm going to visit my brother who is in the army.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찾아가는 쪽에서 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase from the visitor's side.

phrases.en: Visiting hours start at two in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 군대에서 만날 수 있는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the hours when visitors are allowed at hospitals or the military.

phrases.en: It's the intensive care unit right now, so visits aren't allowed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 수 없는 상황을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that visits are not possible.

explain_en: Unlike '만나다' (to meet), it is for going to see someone who cannot freely leave a place, such as the military, a hospital or a prison. People usually say '면회(를) 가다/오다', and the noun is common too, as in '면회 시간' (visiting hours).

examples.en: The masseur carefully loosened my shoulders.
I got a back massage from a masseur.
I am studying to get a massage therapist license.
This masseur has really strong hands.
There is a well-known masseur in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 안마사께 조금 더 세게 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked the masseur to press a little harder.

explain: 안마를 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요. 일상에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 많이 써서, 마사지를 해 주는 사람을 '마사지사'라고도 해요. 누군가의 몸을 직접 주물러 주는 사람이라서 '안마기'와는 달리 사람을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The massage therapist loosened my shoulders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 안마사보다 이 말도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also commonly used in daily life instead of 안마사.

phrases.en: I was tired, so I called a masseur to my home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 불러서 서비스를 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you call someone for a service.

phrases.en: I got a neck massage from a professional masseur.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술이 있는 사람임을 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to make clear the person is skilled.

explain_en: It refers to a person who works as a masseur. In daily life people also use the word '마사지', so someone who gives massages may be called a '마사지사'. Unlike '안마기', which is a machine, this word refers to a person.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 회사에 연수생 열 명이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Ten trainees joined our company this year.

examples.ko: 저는 해외 연수생으로 일 년 동안 일본에 있었어요.
examples.en: I was in Japan for a year as an overseas trainee.
The trainees receive training every morning.
I'm still a trainee, so there's a lot I don't know yet.
I explained the company rules to the trainee.

examples.ko: 한국어 연수생을 위한 수업이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: There are separate classes for Korean-language trainees.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 일을 배우거나, 어학연수처럼 일정 기간 교육을 받는 사람이에요. '연수'가 교육을 받는 일을 뜻해서 '연수를 받다'와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I also became a trainee this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육을 받는 사람이 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone became a person receiving training.

phrases.example: 저는 한 달 동안 회사에서 연수를 받았어요.
phrases.en: I received training at the company for a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연수생'이 하는 일을 동사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes in verb form what a trainee does.

phrases.en: The company is recruiting trainees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 뽑는 공고에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in job or program announcements.

explain_en: Person in a company or institution's training program (신입 연수생) It means someone who learns the work at a company or institution, or takes a training program for a set period such as language study abroad. Since '연수' means training, it often appears with '연수를 받다'.

t90.ax: Ten trainees joined our company this year.

examples.en: The company invited overseas buyers to the event.
The university invites a famous writer.
We will invite only family to the wedding.
I sent an invitation letter to the guests.

examples.ko: 외국에서 온 손님을 공식 만찬에 초청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to invite a guest from abroad to the official dinner.

examples.ko: 선생님이 우리를 저녁 식사에 초청해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher invited us to dinner.

explain: 행사나 모임에 정식으로 부를 때 써요. 친구를 집에 부르는 가벼운 상황에서는 '초대하다'를 써요. 명사는 '초청장', '초청 강연'처럼 붙여요.

phrases.en: I received an invitation to a company event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 초청받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person invited.

phrases.en: I sent invitations to the guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 행사에서 부르는 편지나 카드를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a formal letter or card for an event.

phrases.en: Thank you so much for inviting me today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 모임에 불러 준 사람에게 고마움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to thank someone who invited you to an event or gathering.

explain_en: It is used for formally inviting someone to an event or gathering. For a light situation, such as asking a friend to your home, use '초대하다'. The noun attaches in words like '초청장' (invitation card) and '초청 강연' (invited lecture).

t90.ax: Our teacher invited us to dinner.

examples.en: There is an alumni get-together this weekend.
The company is collecting dues for the social club.
I met my seniors after a long time at the get-together.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 친목회는 한 달에 한 번 모여요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood social club meets once a month.
I'm busy these days because I took on the role of treasurer of the social club.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 이름은 친목회지만 실제로는 사업 이야기만 해요.
examples.en: That group is called a social club, but they only talk business.

explain: 서로 친해지려고 모이는 모임이에요. 같은 취미로 모이는 '동호회', 같은 학교 출신이 모이는 '동창회'와 달리 특별한 조건 없이 가볍게 모여요. '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 한 달에 한 번 친목회를 열어요.
phrases.en: Our team holds a social gathering once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임을 만들어 진행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when organizing and holding the gathering.

phrases.en: I'm going to a get-together this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참석하는 사람의 입장에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the attendee's point of view.

phrases.example: 친목회 회비는 한 달에 만 원이에요.
phrases.en: The social club fee is 10,000 won a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 내는 돈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the money paid to the group.

explain_en: It is a group that meets just to get closer to each other. Unlike a '동호회' (hobby club) or '동창회' (alumni association), it often has no special condition. You say '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'.
